proposals.rule: If the specification mentions an 'always block' (combinational or sequential) that assigns to an output, declare that output as logic (or reg) in the module port list.
proposals.summary: Add conditional rule to declare outputs driven by always blocks as logic/reg.
proposals.reasoning: Several failures (Prob026_alwaysblock1, Prob054_edgedetect, Prob075_counter_2bc) involved compile errors because outputs assigned inside always blocks were not declared as reg/logic. The rule is conditional on the spec mentioning an always block, so it only affects designs that need it and avoids breaking purely combinational assign-only designs.

proposals.tool_code:
# tool: unassigned_output_checker
import re

def run(spec: str, verilog: str, ports: list[dict]) -> dict:
    # Find all output ports
    output_names = {p['name'] for p in ports if p['direction'] == 'output'}
    if not output_names:
        return {'fired': False, 'findings': []}
    # Simple check: look for procedural assignments to outputs inside always/initial blocks
    # We'll approximate by searching for patterns like 'always @' or 'always_ff' or 'always_comb' 
    # followed by a block that contains a variable assignment to an output without being in an if/else that covers all cases.
    # For simplicity, we flag if an output appears in the sensitivity list of an always block but never gets a blocking/nonblocking assignment.
    # This is a heuristic; it will fire only when there is a clear missing assignment.
    fired = False
    findings = []
    # Remove comments and strings to avoid false positives
    def remove_comments_and_strings(text):
        # remove /* ... */
        text = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', '', text, flags=re.DOTALL)
        # remove // ...
        text = re.sub(r'//.*', '', text)
        # remove string literals
        text = re.sub(r'".*?"', '', text)
        text = re.sub(r"'.*?'", '', text)
        return text
    clean = remove_comments_and_strings(verilog)
    # Find all always/initial blocks
    block_pattern = r'(always\s*@\s*\([^)]*\)|always_ff|always_comb|always_latch|initial)\s*([^{]*)\{([^}]*)\}'
    for match in re.finditer(block_pattern, clean, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL):
        block_inner = match.group(3)
        # Find assignments in this block: variable = ... ; or variable <= ... ;
        assigned = set(re.findall(r'\b([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*(=|<=)', block_inner))
        assigned_vars = {v for v, _ in assigned}
        # Check which outputs are in the block's sensitivity (approx: if output name appears in block header)
        header = match.group(2)
        for out in output_names:
            if out in header and out not in assigned_vars:
                fired = True
                findings.append(f'Output {out} appears in always block header but may not be assigned in all paths.')
    return {'fired': fired, 'findings': findings}

proposals.summary: Increase max debug attempts from 2 to 3 to allow more fixing iterations.
proposals.reasoning: Many failing designs required multiple debug cycles to resolve subtle logic errors (e.g., Prob016_m2014_q4j, Prob057_kmap2, Prob063_review2015_shiftcount). Allowing one extra attempt gives the debugger more opportunity to correct mistakes without overburdening the system.
